PullRequest.Title: Engineering - enable automatic retries for failed Electron unit test files
PullRequest.Body:

Enable automatic reruns of failed Electron unit test files in pull request CI to recover from flaky failures without hiding them.

- Add `--rerun-failed-files <count>` to rerun only failed files in a fresh Electron window/renderer. Default runs remain unchanged; debugging and coverage runs do not retry.
- Enable two reruns in the macOS, Linux, and Windows PR workflows, with a 25-minute Electron test step timeout.
- Preserve per-attempt JUnit results and emit CI warnings for files that recover, including when other files still fail.
- Fail after the retry budget is exhausted, and do not retry failures that cannot be attributed to a test file.
- Keep Node.js and browser runners unchanged.

## Validation

- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/event.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/common/lifecycle.test.ts --rerun-failed-files 2 --reporter dot` — passed, 124 tests.
- Five real Electron fixture scenarios — passed: all-pass, flaky recovery, mixed recovered/persistent failures, retries disabled, and root-hook failure. Verified exit codes, fresh renderer PIDs, passing files not rerun, separate XML reports for every attempt, and flaky warnings on both successful and failed runs. Temporary fixtures were removed afterward.
- `node --check test/unit/electron/index.js` and `node --check test/unit/electron/renderer.js` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- test/unit/electron/index.js test/unit/electron/renderer.js` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Validation was performed locally on macOS. Windows/Linux execution and the full Electron suite remain for CI.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The workflow timeout change is explicit, `scripts/test.sh` runs one Electron process synchronously, and `index.js` cannot enter its retry loop until the renderer emits `all done`. Thus a hung attempt receives no retry benefit from the extra ten minutes. The only uncertainty is how often the suite hangs, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: hosted CI runner time and live Electron subprocesses
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is a fixed additional 10 minutes for each hung platform invocation; with the same timeout increase on Linux, macOS, and Windows, aggregate waste can reach 30 runner-minutes per affected PR run.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased failure-path CI latency and retained runner capacity
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The Electron step was forcibly canceled after 15 minutes, bounding a no-progress test process and allowing the workflow to release its runner sooner.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A non-terminating Electron test invocation now retains the hosted runner and Electron process for up to 25 minutes before GitHub Actions cancels it, instead of 15 minutes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `timeout-minutes: 25` on the Electron test step replaces the previous 15-minute cap; the same increase is made in the Darwin and Windows PR workflows.
Findings.Title: Preserve the 15-minute watchdog for hung attempts
Findings.Impact: When an Electron test deadlocks or otherwise stops making progress, PR CI and all later steps in that platform job are delayed by an additional 10 minutes while the hosted runner and Electron processes remain occupied. The same change on all three OS workflows can consume up to 30 extra runner-minutes for a cross-platform hang.
Findings.Evidence: `.github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml:311` raises the outer watchdog from 15 to 25 minutes. `scripts/test.sh:47` synchronously launches Electron, while `test/unit/electron/index.js:628` awaits the attempt's `done` promise and the renderer only sends `all done` after Mocha completes (`test/unit/electron/renderer.js:487`). Therefore a deadlocked renderer/test never reaches the new retry logic and simply occupies the runner until the enlarged workflow timeout expires.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the 25-minute total budget for completed retries, but add a per-attempt no-progress/watchdog timeout (at most the prior 15-minute bound) in the Electron runner, or otherwise separate retry headroom from the hang timeout so a stuck first attempt is terminated promptly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal PR Electron unit-test run with all files passing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Electron startup, renderer load, selected module imports, Mocha execution, IPC event delivery, and reporter drain are sequentially on the test-step critical path. On success the loop exits after one attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch Electron and create the test BrowserWindow/renderer process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Electron renderer process for an all-pass run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Electron renderer process was launched for the same all-pass scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The renderer must initialize and complete all selected tests before the step progresses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Structured-clone and send `runnable.file` with runnable events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Mocha lifecycle events produce several IPC messages per test/hook; the diff adds one module-path string to runnable payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events crossed IPC without the `file` property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: IPC reporting occurs during the run, but the incremental bounded string field does not establish a material regression relative to existing title/path/error payloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load test modules and write/drain test results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All selected test modules are imported once; one JUnit result file is emitted in PR CI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial run performed the same module loads and emitted one result file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Imports and reporter completion must finish before the attempt resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bind a localhost HTTP server for remote-resource tests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One localhost server bind per Electron invocation; requests occur only in tests that exercise the remote-resource fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same server was started once for the Electron invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server startup precedes test execution; fixture requests affect only their tests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of selected test modules and Mocha runnable events in the Electron suite.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer attempt runs at a time. Module imports in `loadModules` are serialized; retries are also serialized. The three platform workflows may execute independently in CI.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each Electron renderer is intentionally fresh; the initial run and every retry reload selected modules without a cross-window module cache. Retry selection is deduplicated by `Set`, and no concurrent requests require coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the all-pass call path remains one renderer attempt and the added metadata is visible on every runnable IPC payload.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact suite test count and IPC-byte increase were not measured, but the added field is bounded by existing runnable event cardinality and does not by itself justify a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no extra renderer, module-load pass, or result-file write occurs on the normal all-pass path; the IPC metadata increase is minor and bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Attributed flaky or persistently failing test files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a completed failing attempt, reporter drain finishes, a fresh BrowserWindow is created, the previous one is destroyed, and only failed files are imported and executed. Up to two retries are on the PR test-step critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a fresh BrowserWindow/renderer for each retry and destroy the prior window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial renderer plus at most two fresh renderer processes, only after attributed test-file failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A completed failing first attempt exited without creating another renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each retry startup and failed-file test execution extends the failed/flaky test step before its final result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload only failed test modules in each fresh renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One import per distinct failed file per retry; successful files are excluded and failures are deduplicated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No second import pass occurred after a failing run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold imports and tests for the failed subset must finish before the next decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write a distinct result file for each retry attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional JUnit XML file for each retry attempt, at most two in PR CI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the initial JUnit file was written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter drain is awaited before moving to the next attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Relay retry attempt events and collect distinct failed files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Mocha lifecycle IPC traffic for tests/hooks in the failed-file subset on each retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Events feed the reporters and failure-file tracking during each sequential attempt.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct failed files after per-attempt deduplication, their transitive module/test cost, and the configured retry cap of two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one attempt runs at a time; retries are sequential and capped at two in PR CI. Within an attempt, failed modules are loaded serially. There is no aggregate process burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every retry uses a new renderer and cold module graph by design. Failed file paths are deduplicated per attempt with a `Set`; only currently failing files are selected on the next attempt, so passing files are not reloaded again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loop, cap, failed-file deduplication, cold BrowserWindow construction, reporter drain, and sequential scheduling are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Flake frequency and failed-file test size vary, so the added wall time ranges from one small-file rerun to two cold reruns of a larger failed subset.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the repeated work is the feature's explicit, bounded tradeoff, operates only on the deduplicated failed subset, and avoids concurrent renderer bursts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron test attempt hangs or stops making progress
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shell waits synchronously for Electron; `index.js` awaits the renderer's `all done` event. A deadlock or no-progress renderer blocks all later job steps until the workflow timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the Electron test process under the enlarged workflow timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One non-terminating Electron invocation per affected platform, retained for up to 25 rather than 15 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub Actions canceled and cleaned up the same no-progress invocation after 15 minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It blocks the remainder of that platform job and occupies its hosted runner for ten additional minutes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Keep the local remote-resource server alive while awaiting test completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One localhost test server and its associated Electron resources remain live with the stuck invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The resources were retained only until the prior 15-minute cancellation bound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These resources remain retained until workflow cancellation; they do not enable progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of platform workflows experiencing a no-progress Electron invocation; the fixed increase is ten runner-minutes per platform.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One stuck Electron process per affected platform workflow; Linux, macOS, and Windows workflows can retain runners independently. No retry executes because attempts are sequential and completion-gated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A hung attempt never completes, so no retry selection, cache behavior, or coalescing is reached. The single renderer remains live until the outer workflow watchdog cancels it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the outer timeout changed from 15 to 25 minutes, while retries are reached only after `done` resolves.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of full renderer/test deadlocks is unknown, but workflow timeouts exist for this realistic failure mode; the additional latency and runner occupancy are exactly ten minutes whenever it occurs.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity cleanup/latency regression: retry headroom was added by extending the only hang watchdog, although a hung attempt cannot use retries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Debug, coverage, and unattributed completed-failure runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These modes retain a single Electron renderer execution. Coverage collection/reporting or the development window behavior remains the dominant path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run debug, coverage, or unattributed-failure execution in one renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same single-attempt critical path as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect precise V8 coverage through Electron debugger commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Coverage debugger IPC/snapshots occur at their existing test-driven cardinality; retries are disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coverage IPC occurred once, with no retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Coverage snapshots and report generation remain on the coverage critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected tests and pre-existing coverage snapshot frequency; retry count is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer window; no retry concurrency or repeated cold starts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Coverage explicitly forces zero reruns; development mode creates one window and returns. Unattributed completed failures also stop without retrying.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the guards are explicit in the changed control flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for retry multiplicity because these branches explicitly disable or bypass retries.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression from retry work because these modes do not create retry attempts.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and their renderer, launcher, reporter, workflow, IPC, filesystem, network, and process-lifecycle paths. Submitted one medium-severity finding for extending the no-progress subprocess watchdog; the retry execution itself is sequential, deduplicated, cold by design, and bounded to two PR-CI reruns.
